paragraphs: Some people think students having the best academic performances should be rewarded by school, others argue that hard-work and showing great improvement ones are more deserve to these gifts. Personally, I strongly believe that both top and high-motivation students have abilities to be rewarded.

On the one hand, admittedly, rewarding top-grade students is undeniably justified. Initially, having diligently applied themselves to their studies, those students deserve their praises and privileges, which may encourages they and others to study harder to win the rewards, propel overall academic gains. Furthermore, this kind of competition is seen in almost every aspect of life, where only the best individual are rewarded. Being used to this reality and thriving in the face of fierce competition, students are able to achieve success in later life.

On the other hand, however, it is equally important to rewarding students having significant developments. Firstly, since only a few smart students can come first and receive the rewards, others may think that their effort is futile. Because they can not surpass those outstanding individuals, they prone to feeling overwhelmed and disheartened and gradually lose the incentive to study. Moreover, emphasizing improvements, school can encourage all student to be diligent in their studies and help them to understand what they need to constantly improve themselves, irrespective of how well they have been or are performing. The constant desire to outdo themselves is even benefit themselves more than the competitive determination to win against all others.
In conclusion, I am firmly convinced that school should reward not only the best students but also others thriving in their studies.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that public museums and art galleries will play an essential role in the community no more due to the thrive and convenience of internet. However, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, technology nowadays provide people a beneficial way to experience culture and historic by their own. Consisting of high-resolution images, three-dimensional reconstructions and virtual reality platforms, the internet and modern systems enable viewers to explore masterpieces or ancient artefacts in remarkable detail, without leaving home. This can be easily seen in the way some popular museums in the world offer viewers both online and offline experiences of their diverse artworks and historical items by using cutting edge technology for those people who cannot afford and have mobility issues, can still access a vast range of cultural and historical heritages.

However, I strongly believe that public museums and art galleries will still necessary for several reasons. Chief of them is; online experience, cannot replicate the direct sensory engagement of seeing an artefact or artwork in person, which can evokes emotions and a sense of authenticity that images cannot convey. A popular example is Viet Nam, a country renowned for it long and adorable history, which being saved and conveyed through countless generations by its cultural and historical heritages. Furthermore, these traditional services, is vital cultural hubs, it play and pivotal role in symbolizing the identity of a region. This is a magnet for tourism and a facilitator of bonding within the community.
In conclusion, I strongly convinced that despite the convenience and popular of the internet and modern technology, the role of cultural hubs like public museums or art galleries is undeniable.

review.overall: Em giữ lập trường phản đối và hai thân bài đúng chức năng; ý về Việt Nam là điểm riêng. Nhưng ví dụ này chưa cho thấy trải nghiệm trực tiếp đem lại điều gì khác hình ảnh trên mạng. Câu công nghệ kéo dài, gộp online/offline với người khó chi trả; các khung “will still necessary”, “can evokes” và “I strongly convinced” đều sai ở mức động từ nền đã học. Bài còn ẩu ở khâu tự soát. Em cần nghiêm túc, cầu thị viết lại từng câu được đánh dấu, thêm cơ chế cảm xúc cho ví dụ Việt Nam và kiểm toàn bộ động từ trước khi nộp.

paragraphs: There is an opinion that public museums and art galleries will become unnecessary as the growth and convenience of the internet enable people to see historical objects and works of art on a computer. However, I am of the opposite school of thought.

Admittedly, technology nowadays provides people with a beneficial way to experience culture and history on their own. This can be seen when some museums offer online experiences of their diverse artworks and historical items through cutting-edge technology. paragraphs: Some people believe that children should be free to make mistakes whereas others argue that adults have the responsibility to measure them to not make mistakes. Personally, I am of the first school of thought, provided that errors do not involve serious danger.

On the one hand, opponents of a trial and error approach often emphasise some reasons for their beliefs. Firstly, according to them, most mistakes are avoidable, such as playing with fire, knives, and electricity, which are unnecessary to get hurt to learn to be careful. Secondly, it is the responsibility for parents to shield their children from harm, ultimately forestalling their mistakes and fulfilling this duty. Moreover, being pre-emptively help children, adults can enjoy their peace of mind and do their best to protect and raise their child.

However, Those on the other side also have their own valid reasoning. Chief of them is, it is impossible to make sure that children will have no mistake given that parents cannot be all around themself all the time. Living their own lives, children experience with new things and make mistakes is inevitable. Furthermore, by having freedom to try and fail, children will learn invaluable lesson, which will ultimately stand them in good stead in later stages of life. Added to this is that, they will become more independent from making mistakes. If being shielded from everything, they will grow up overdependent on others, which is a undesirable trait.

In conclusion, it seems to me that despite we can control children's actions at a certain extent to prevent them from making mistakes, allowing children to learn from them is a good preparation for the future, provided that parents need to give guidance on important matters to prevent them errors that may derail their future.

paragraphs: Some people believe that children should be free to make mistakes, whereas others argue that adults have a responsibility to help them avoid making mistakes. Personally, I am of the first school of thought, provided that the errors do not involve serious danger.

On the one hand, opponents of a trial-and-error approach often emphasise several reasons for their view. Firstly, according to them, most mistakes are avoidable. Children do not need to get hurt while playing with fire, knives or electricity to learn to be careful. Secondly, parents have a responsibility to shield their children from harm; forestalling their mistakes helps fulfil this duty. Moreover, by helping children pre-emptively, adults can enjoy their peace of mind, knowing that they have done their best to protect and raise their child.

However, those on the other side also have their own valid reasoning. Chief among their arguments is that it is impossible to ensure that children never make mistakes, given that parents cannot be around their children all the time. Living their own lives, children experiment with new things, making some mistakes inevitable. Furthermore, by having the freedom to try and fail, children will learn invaluable lessons, which will stand them in good stead later in life. Added to this is that they may become more independent by making mistakes. If shielded from everything, they may grow up overdependent on others, which is an undesirable trait.

In conclusion, it seems to me that although we can control children's actions to a certain extent, allowing children to learn from mistakes is good preparation for the future, provided that parents give guidance on important matters to help them avoid errors that may derail their future.

WRITING TASK 2
You should spend about 40 minutes on this task.
Some people say history is one of the most important school subjects. Other people think that, in today’s world, subjects like science and technology are more important than history. Discuss both these views and give your own opinion.
Give reasons for your answer and include any relevant examples from your knowledge or experience.

paragraphs: Some people argue that the most crucial compulsory subjects is history. Many others think it no longer true nowadays and subjects like science or technology are more necessary. Personally, I am of the first school of thought.

Admittedly, the impact of modern subjects is undeniable for several reasons. Chief of them is, those subjects help learner gain diverse and quality career opportunities, especially in this modernization and globalization. Advocator of the later school of thought is true at a certain extent when it almost impossible to become a skilled engineering or a teacher without an academic lisence. This can be easily seen in the way almost every Asian parents always hope their childrens have a perfect academic performances or attend a top university; for them, academic certificates is the most important driver of achievement, which lea easily leading to a stable and successful future. They also note that subjects like science and technology help students develop a critical thinking, which helps us thrive in the future due to logic and creative thinking.

However, I strongly believe that, without any doubts, historic is consistently is the most pivotal subjects for both country and students for its massive and variety advantages. On the one hand, this subject help every nations remain its identity and independent. History of a country consist of its culture, story and its milestones, which makes it unique and become the heart of a country. Without an own history, a country would loss it beautiful and destinations, seriously causing to extinct of it and what it's people have done for million years. On the other hand, by learning history, students can explore why them is live today and remember historical things happened to their ancestor, their country and all the world. By respect the ancestors and learning historic by heart, students foster their love of countries and understanding what make their countries unique, which help them become the leaders of their countries in the future.
In conclusion, I strongly convinced that, despite modern subjects today is very important to learn, historic is still play the most crucial role in each countries.

Đoạn lịch sử có ý về bản sắc nhưng đang khẳng định quá mạnh rằng không có lịch sử thì một quốc gia sẽ biến mất. Em hãy dùng một ví dụ cụ thể và sửa “historic” thành “history” khi nói tên môn học.

paragraphs.text: Some people consider history the most important school subject, whereas others give greater priority to science and technology. I agree that history deserves particular attention, although students also need a sound education in modern scientific subjects.

Science and technology offer clear benefits. Studying them can teach pupils to test evidence, solve problems and use digital tools responsibly. These skills are relevant to careers in engineering, teaching and healthcare, but their value is not limited to employment. For example, a student who understands basic scientific reasoning can evaluate a health claim instead of accepting it without evidence. Schools should therefore keep science and technology in the curriculum and provide students with opportunities to apply what they learn.

I nevertheless believe history has a special role in helping young people understand their communities. Learning how earlier generations responded to conflict or social change can give students a fuller view of the institutions they live with today. It can also help them recognise that people experienced past events in different ways. When pupils investigate local history, for instance, they may see why a place or tradition matters to their families and neighbours. This understanding can strengthen civic responsibility and respect for cultural heritage. History does not guarantee national independence or turn every student into a leader, but it gives them knowledge with which to take part thoughtfully in society.

In conclusion, science and technology provide valuable practical skills, while history helps students understand the people and choices that shaped their country. Both should be taught, yet I would give history a strong place in school because its lessons support informed and responsible citizenship.
